title: Knowing everyone, from Nat King Cole to Lena Horne
summary: Looking back he says he has been close to nearly every musician and entertainer, recalling Nat King Cole as a pianist in California and Lena Horne in the Cotton Club chorus.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: In looking back over your career, all the people you've known and played with, you know, what are some of the things that stand out in your mind, some of the people you've known?

Well, being like I am, I'm always -- I'm a guy that thinks a lot and reminisce a lot -- the whole, everybody, I mean, I could -- I mean, it's been just like I have a million friends, and they're all scattered every place, all in really music business, and I've been close friends to everybody from the singers like Virginia Rustian and on down. I mean anybody you name, it seems funny, and it seems funny for a person to say that they've been contacted with most everybody, but I have. I've played with and worked and been close to mostly every musician and every entertainer and singer that has ever amounted to anything.
That goes for Nat King Cole. I remember when he was

-- came to California, and I had my band out there, and he, you know, came out there with a show. And he wasn't doing anything, you know. In fact, I remember when he organized his first group. He never sang at all. He was a great piano player, fine pianist.

And we worked together out there in California, and when I come back, first thing I know, he had a trio, and the next thing I know he was singing and became a big star, you know. And Billy Daniels, everybody that you could name I've been contacted in the music business somewhere along the line either writing for them or playing with them or working with them.

In fact, Cab Calloway had mostly everybody at that time that was working with us doing theaters and shows. So just about any -- that goes for Bill Robinson, goes for Lena Horne. I mean, I knew her when she was in the Cotton Club chorus, and that goes for anybody you can name in the show business. I can tell you something about, you know, my relationships with them.
